item.title: Authority Pages Beat Competitor Copying
item.description: The goal of competitor research is not to imitate page titles. It is to find unanswered buyer questions and build a clearer, deeper, more useful website around them.

item.title: Customer-Facing Pages Should Not Show the Strategy
item.description: Good website strategy should be felt by the visitor, not explained to them. The page should answer buyer questions clearly without exposing internal labels like SEO, AI search, content architecture, or conversion strategy.

item.title: Manufacturing Websites Need Specs, Not Slogans
item.description: The best manufacturing websites are not the prettiest ones. They are the clearest ones. Buyers and AI search systems both need specifics: what you make, what materials you handle, what dimensions you can support, and how someone gets a quote.

item.title: We Ran a Real GEO Audit. The Score Was 56/100. Here's What That Means.
item.description:
We ran a full GEO audit on a modern SaaS + hardware site this week. Four dimensions scored independently, then weighted into a composite. The final score: 56/100 — Grade C: Developing.

Here’s the breakdown that actually surprised us — and what it means for any business trying to get cited by AI search engines.

The Four Dimensions (And How They Were Weighted)

item.title: What a 4-Dimensional AI Visibility Audit Actually Looks Like
item.description: Technical. Content. Schema. Brand. A real AI visibility audit measures all four — and the breakdown tells you more than the total score. Here’s what each dimension measures and the common patterns we see.

item.title: The Google vs. Everyone Else GEO Problem
item.description: Don’t drop llms.txt just because Google said it’s optional. Google is one AI platform out of many — and the most forgiving one. Optimize for the hardest crawler and everything else gets covered.

item.title: Wikidata: The Free AI Citation Multiplier Nobody Told Local Businesses About
item.description: ChatGPT cites Wikidata in ~47.9% of responses. Most local businesses aren’t on it. A 20-minute entry plus a sameAs embed in your schema is one of the highest-leverage things you can do for AI visibility right now.

item.title: From 35 to 93: What Actually Moves Structured Data Scores for Local Businesses
item.description: A single LocalBusiness block was the standard in 2015. In 2026, AI systems need a complete identity layer — Organization, FAQPage, Article with Speakable, Person, BreadcrumbList, and sameAs arrays. Here’s what that actually looks like.
